lines.text: Four agents in four terminals. One finished an hour ago. One is stuck. One has waited forty minutes for your yes.
Agent R Q puts every agent on one screen. What it's doing, what it needs, and every command it ran.
Each workspace gets a card, naming its agent. The dot is green while it's connected. Yellow chips count what waits on you.
The Kanban board puts every task on one board. Nothing needs a refresh. When billing's export is done, its card moves itself.
Billing's agent wants to run a migration. The request comes to you, with the exact command.
Allow it once, always, or deny it. The buttons are right on its board card.
Docs needs a decision, so it marks its task blocked. You answer in its thread, and it picks up where it stopped.
Open a task, and you see it working: for how long, and its last three tools.
Type while it works, and your message reaches it at once. No restart.
Every task keeps a timeline. Red is time blocked. Yellow is time waiting on you. And the totals add it up.
And every command is on the record. Trajectory shows each call, and who said yes. Like this force push to main: denied.
Every agent, on one screen. What do you check first when an agent goes quiet? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
